header_sentences: See Arrow-snake, Asp, Cockatrice, Dragon, Fire-serpent, and Viper.

contexts.text: The Sensuous is represented by the serpent. AC 192. AC 194.

The Most Ancients... called the sensuous things of man serpents; because, as serpents are nearest the earth, so are sensuous things nearest the body. Hence, reasonings from sensuous things concerning the mysteries of faith, they called poisons of a serpent; and the reasoners themselves, serpents; and as such reason much from sensuous or visible things... it is said that the serpent was more cunning than every beast of the field. Illustrated.
Hence the proverb... that the serpent stoppeth the ear.
Those were called serpents who trusted in sensuous more than in revealed things. At this day it is still worse...
Such are not only deaf serpents, but also flying serpents. Described.
A serpent (most anciently) = circumspection, and thus the Sensuous by which they exorcised it... Hence, the words, Be ye prudent as serpents...AC 6398:3. AE 581:9.
The brazen serpent = the Sensuous of the Lord... who alone exercises circumspection and provides for all; and therefore those who looked on it were saved. ( = the Lord, and protection. AC 8624:end.)
These are the serpents who seduce the world. Described.
(Thus) the Sensuous, which is the serpent, cursed itself... Treated of.

Jehovah God said unto the serpent () = that they perceived their Sensuous to be the cause. That the serpent was cursed above every beast... = that the Sensuous averted itself from the Celestial and turned itself to the Corporeal, and thus cursed itself. That the serpent should walk upon its belly = that the Sensuous could no longer look upward to celestial, but downward to corporeal and earthly things. That it should eat dust all the days of its life = that the Sensuous had become so that it could not live from anything but what is corporeal and earthly. AC 244. AC 245. AC 247. AC 249. AE 581:10.

I will put enmity between thee and the woman... ()... The serpent, here, = all evil in general; in special, the love of self... The head of the serpent = the dominion of evil in general, and of the love of self in special... AC 251, Explained, Illustrated. AC 257. AC 8678. Explained.
The seed of the serpent = all infidelity. Explained.
The serpent can injure only the lowest natural things; and not, unless it is a species of viper, interior natural things in man, still less spiritual things, and least of all celestial things...
The brazen serpent = the Lord's sensuous and natural good. ( = the Lord as to the external Sensuous, or Natural. AC 3863:5. AR 49:end.)
A place where large-bellied serpents inflict torment with their bites. SE 1495.
A lake containing monstrous serpents, with pestilent breath.
This Hell is sometimes changed into direful serpents, which bite them...
(Such deceitful ones) seem to themselves to live among serpents... which torture them. SE 2857.
Their eyes are serpentine, having, as is said, the sight and its idea present on all sides. SE 4019.
The serpent's root () = scientifics.
The love of self is the head of the serpent.
(Such) were called serpents of the tree of knowledge. Explained. AC 4802:4. AC 5128:3. AC 10236:6. DP 310. TCR 324. TCR 380:4. TCR 402:12.
The serpent of brass was holy in the time of Moses; but, when the external was worshipped, it became profane...
A serpent appears wound around (those who practise communion of wives). SE 2867.
Serpent (biting horse's heels) = one who reasons from sensuous and scientific things about Divine arcana. AC 3923:2. AC 6400, Explained.
The broad way was bordered with trees and flowers... in which were hidden snakes and serpents...
This conjunction with the Lord as to His Divine Sensuous, is represented by those reviving from the bite of the serpents who looked on the brazen serpent. (). Explained.
The deceitful appear as serpents; and the most deceitful as vipers.
The cuticles (of those who have been deceitful) appear like conglutinations of mere serpents.
Dan shall be a serpent upon the way () = their ratiocination concerning truth, because good does not yet lead. A serpent = ratiocination from the Sensuous. AC 6398:2. Explained.
Elsewhere, malice, cunning, and deceit, are signified by serpents, but poisonous ones, as vipers. The ratiocination of these is poison.
Their ratiocinations about truth and good are called serpents, cockatrices ().

(Moses' rod) became a serpent () = the sensuous and corporeal man separate from the internal; for a serpent = a man who reasons from sensuous things; thus the Sensuous of man; and, as a serpent = the Sensuous, it also = the Corporeal; for the Sensuous has what belongs to it from the senses of the body; and, as the Sensuous, regarded in itself, is such as (here) described, it = all evil in general. (Further explained.)
Moses fled from before it = horror at the separated Sensuous. Explained.
Take it by the tail = the power of elevating from the ultimate of the Sensuous. Explained.

As the serpent = the separated Sensuous, and the derivative ratiocination from the fallacies of the senses concerning the truths of faith, the tail of the serpent = the falsity itself; for this is the ultimate or lowest... Illustrated.
The rod becoming a serpent = that they would become completely sensuous and corporeal.
That mere fallacies would begin to reign with them, whence falsities, is described by the serpent into which Aaron's rod was turned ().
It shall become a water serpent () = that mere fallacies, and the derivative falsities, will reign with them. Explained. AC 7295, Explained.
A water serpent is the same in the Hebrew as a whale. Illustrated.
Water serpents = the falsities themselves from fallacies from which are reasonings, and through which are perversions.
Serpents = the falsities from which are reasonings. Illustrated. The same are signified by dragons. Explained.
The first degree of the deprivation of the influx of truth and good is described by Aaron's rod being turned into a serpent...
(The magicians' rods) became water serpents () = dulness as to the apperception of truth; (for) water serpents = falsities from fallacies. Explained.
The serpent (in Genesis) = ratiocination from the intellectual proprium. AC 9942:3.
When inspected by the Angels (Genii) appear like serpents; for they have the nature of serpents, and that which goes forth from them is spiritual venom.
Venomous serpents, as asps, cockatrices, vipers, = the deceitful. Illustrated.
Serpents and scorpions () = evils, and falsities of evil: to tread on them = to destroy them.

They seem to themselves to be bound hand and foot with serpents... For the corporeal Sensuous is there represented by serpents; and therefore serpents, in the Word, = the Sensuous, which is the ultimate of man's life. SE 1668.
They cast themselves on the ground, and writhe like a serpent. AE 865.
They appear to themselves to creep away like serpents.
This love (of exercising command) is the serpent which deceived Eve and Adam... TCR 822.
This worst evil is meant by the head of the serpent...
They made images of serpents... because serpents = the prudence of the sensuous man (and also his cunning. TCR 205.)
From the serpent's root a basilisk () = from the conceit of Own intelligence the destruction of all truth with them.
Such (evil uses) are venomous serpents, etc.
Compared to the lascivious delights... of serpents in stenches.

Man's proprium, which is his will... is that serpent which seduced our first parents, of which it is said: I will put enmity between thee and the woman... The serpent = evil of every kind; its head = the love of self. Further Explained. DP 241.

As the Ancients called the sensuous man a serpent, and such a man is crafty, cunning, and a clever reasoner above others, it is said that the serpent was made more cunning than every beast of the field; and the Lord said, Be ye prudent as serpents... AR 455:end.
The serpent (in Eden) = the Sensuous and the proprium of man, which in itself is the love of self and the conceit of Own intelligence, thus the devil and Satan. DP 313:3.
Writhes like a serpent placed before a fire. AR 611:2. AR 676:4. CL 10:5.
They are like serpents in the grass...
Their tails were like unto serpents... () = that they are sensuous and inverted...

By serpents, in the Word, are signified sensuous things... for affections merely sensuous appear there like serpents. The reason is that serpents creep on the ground, and lick the dust; and sensuous things are the lowest ones of the understanding and will; for they stand forth next the world, and are nourished from its objects and delights... Noxious serpents, which are of many kinds, = the sensuous things which are dependent on evil affections, which make the interiors of the mind with those who are insane from falsities of evil; and harmless serpents = the sensuous things which are dependent on good affections which make the interiors of the mind with those who are wise from truths of good. Illustrated.

One who does not acknowledge the Lord is not admitted into Heaven, but stands below, and is bitten by serpents, that is, by infernal Spirits, from which there is no healing except that which came to the sons of Israel by their looking to the brazen serpent, by which is meant the Lord as to the Divine Human.
A serpent = man sensuous from the Corporeal.
A serpent = those who seduce. Illustrated.
The serpent cast out of his mouth water as a flood after the woman () = ratiocinations from falsities in abundance to destroy the Church. Explained. See AE 763.
Because they think sensuously and not spiritually about the Things of faith, they are called the old serpent (). Explained.
The serpent (in Genesis) = the devil as to the love of self and the conceit of Own intelligence; and this love is the possessor of the tree of knowledge. CL 353:2.
His feet in a basket full of serpents...
Red serpents crept up the sides of the glowing donkey...
The lascivious delights of scortatory love are presented under the forms of serpents, etc.
About the cavern lay a great serpent in spiral folds, which breathed poison into it.
A lake in which were some red serpents.
Like one who sees a serpent in the way... and seizes hold of its head...
He is tortured like a serpent laid on sheets of hot iron, or on an ant-hill. TCR 578:end.
A devil seen like a great serpent, writhing in agony...
She dissolved into serpents, or horrible snakes, and was thus rejected.

On a certain kind of serpent. - There are genera and species of those who are serpents, or who (here) had been deceitful. In the other life they are called serpents, because they appear like serpents to the Angels; for, when the Angels inspect them, they are as it were turned into serpents before the eyes of Spirits (and also to themselves), insomuch that I supposed them to be completely turned into serpentiform globes... For in serpents there are poisons by which, in nature, are represented deceits. SE 2497. SE 2519. SE 2762. SE 3061. SE 3080. SE 4681:2.
A sorceress, when inspected, was turned into a ball of serpents...
(Gustavus Adolphus was also represented) by a great serpent.
(Their delight) is turned into direful serpents, which gnaw and devour their breasts and genitals...
The assassin [went] into serpentine flexures...
She was punished by a long serpent...
As they still supposed that they perceived interior things, they are called the head of the serpent.
b. His phantasies were represented as serpents.
The evil in the interior sphere cannot be inspected by the Angels, for they would be turned into serpents...
Under Dog, see this reference.
Their ideas [were] as it were a sphere of venomous serpents.
Dragons are flying serpents. AE 714:3. AE 714:5, (Explained.)
There are dragons and serpents (in that new Hell).
It is from this representation that serpents cast their exuviae; for the deceitful are represented by serpents. SE 4356. SE 4366.
Innumerable serpents and vipers (seen) who were evil Spirits.
By phantasies... they project serpents, and the other would grind them up with his feet, so that the gore would appear over the whole plane...
The Jesuits... are represented by serpents of various kinds, viperine; spotted; more, or less, venomous.
In that Hell (of magicians) are direful venomous serpents.
These are the serpents treated of in Genesis.
A certain female was representatively interiorly full of venomous serpents: she supposed that if she could void the serpents as excrement, she would be delivered (from all sin)...
Those who insidiate against conjugial love... when inspected, appear like serpents.

There appeared a great head of a serpent, ugly with its black scales... That magical Hell so appears... because serpents are the natural, and the reasonings from them... (Such) is signified by the great crooked serpent... where Egypt is treated of, where there was magic.
A certain one who... appeared as a groat serpent, which coiled itself round the neck of the other... It was terrific to see. Explained.
First, he was seen as an infant, then as a venomous serpent...

There appeared a great serpent... almost green in colour; it was seen to seize a certain Spirit by the garment, and bring him round to the right... By sensuous things and their fallacies he had so treated others. Explained.
But behind the ears lies hidden a serpent.
There are places (in the Hell of the profane) where there are serpents of various kinds.
She turned herself into various serpentine forms, and (so) penetrated...
Such were called by the Ancients serpents; for they can reason...

Those also are serpents who (here) have lived solitary... and have not divulged their thoughts. Those who have thought evilly about... the neighbour act... like serpents, and, when inspected... appear as serpents...
They (then) represent the ship as surrounded with serpents.
When he thought about confirmations... there appeared serpents, which wanted to fly into his feet.
Thus is the head of the serpent trampled on.
There appeared a great serpent there, thick, like a beam, from which went forth four feet, horrible...
When they are thinking, there is heard a hissing as of serpents...

A serpent = that which is the ultimate of life with man, and is called the external Sensuous. As this ultimate, in the Lord, was Divine, a serpent of brass was made, which signified that if they looked to the Lord's Divine Human, they would revive... AE 581:12. AE 805:10.
Under Leviathan, see this reference. AE 581:8.
A serpent upon the way, and an asp upon the path = the Sensuous as to truth and as to good. (Compare AE 581:11.)
The serpent's root = this false principle (of faith alone). ( = the Sensuous. AE 817:9.)
Under Scorpion, see this reference.
Their tails were like serpents... Serpents = the astutenesses of the sensuous man.
Serpents, in the Word, = the sensuous man as to cunning, and as to prudence. Fully illustrated. AE 581:9.
The serpent was more cunning than any beast... = the sensuous man; in general, the Sensuous itself. Explained. AE 763:end.
Serpents = the affections of the sensuous man, because they crawl... Explained.
Hence the devil, or Hell, is called a serpent. Illustrated.
To tread on serpents = to despise... the wiles, cunning, and wicked arts of the infernal crew. AE 581:7. Illustrated.
The fiery flying serpents = sensuous things...
The Gentiles worshipped serpents, because the serpents the Sensuous... and its prudence.
That they should take up serpents, was said because serpents = the Hells as to malice...
Under Dragon, see this reference.
Serpents = the evils thence.
The old serpent = the sensuous.
They are called serpents; for a serpent = the Sensuous; because this is the lowest of man's life, and as it were creeps... and licks the dust like a serpent.
Their seduction by the serpent = seduction by the Sensuous, which derives everything from the world, and nothing from Heaven. Explained. AE 739:7. AE 739:9. Char 204.
The serpent () = the Sensuous of man, where is his proprium, which in itself is nothing but evil.
The voice of a serpent () = cunning and deceit.
A serpent = infernal evil with those who pervert the truths of the Word, and thereby deceive cunningly and deceitfully.
